Subject: Private offer question: usage thresholds and partner netting

Hi Mateo,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the latency/throughput numbers. Before we go into procurement, Procurement and Channel ops asked two specific things about your Private Offer structure:

1) We plan to hit a lot of headroom in months 4–6. Do you support a tiered discount that triggers automatically once monthly usage crosses a threshold (e.g., 2M tokens/month -> 7% discount, 5M -> 12%)? If so, what evidence is required to trigger retroactive credits?

2) We engage two resellers who need to be carved into the revenue waterfall. Can you show how partner netting (pass-through to reseller) is handled in the private offer? We need clarity on net revenue to reseller vs Redwood-listed price.

Attached is our usage profile (welspring_mop_v2.xlsx) — high initial burst with steady-state growth.

Goal: get a working structure we can hand to procurement this week. Any chance you can sketch the proposal and how credits would be processed?

Best,
Samantha Blake
Head of Cloud Procurement
Welspring Health

From: mateo_alvarez@redwood.ai
To: Samantha Blake <samantha.blake@welspring.com>
Cc: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Aug 2028 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private offer question: usage thresholds and partner netting

Thanks Samantha — useful profile, appreciate the detail. Short answers up front:

- Yes, we can do usage-triggered tiered discounts in a Private Offer. They can be forward-looking (apply to future invoices) and/or backward-looking with a true-up credit at month-end; the latter requires metering evidence (HubSpot deal + invoice reconciliation + monitored token tallies).
- Partner netting is supported: our PO waterfall distinguishes List Price -> Customer Effective Price -> Reseller Netback. We can model reseller pass-through as either (A) percentage of net revenue paid to reseller via Redwood-managed settlement, or (B) customer-side reseller commission (the customer sends a portion). Option A is simpler operationally for large resellers.

I sketched a proposal in-line below — Connor/Irène copied for ops/legal checks.

Proposal sketch (high level):
- Anchors: 0–1.99M tokens: list price (no discount)
  2.0–4.99M: 7% unit discount (auto-apply next invoice)
  5.0M+: 12% unit discount + 1% reseller netback (paid quarterly)
- True-up mechanics: we run daily tallies. If monthly usage crosses a tier, forward discount applies immediately and a month-end invoice credit is posted for retroactive portion. Evidence: token tallies + HubSpot deal ID + signed SOW.
- Reseller handling: Redwood can route a quarterly netback payment to reseller (Option A). We'll include a reseller entity id in the PO and pay via ACH; payments reconciled against the quarterly usage report.

Open items for procurement:
- Acceptable SLA/claim window for requesting retro credits (we typically allow 60 days).
- Exact reseller identity and W9/supplier docs for Redwood payouts.
- Whether Welspring wants credits as account-level credit or direct cash refund.

Connor — can you confirm operational feasibility and whether we need to scope any accounting notes for finance? Irène — anything on compliance/audit trail needs?

Cheers,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior AE, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Thanks — quick operational confirmation from my side.

1) Metering and credits: we can produce a daily token tally export tied to an invoice ID. For retroactive credits, accounting will require: HubSpot deal ID, signed SOW (or PO), token tallies for the relevant month, and a signed credit acceptance form. We can automate the tally -> credit posting pipeline but need legal sign-off on the credit policy (time window and dispute flow).

2) Reseller payments: Option A (Redwood-managed quarterly netback) is doable. We will:
- Maintain a reseller payout ledger (reseller entity, payout %).
- Issue quarterly settlement statements and ACH payments.
- Provide CSV statements to Welspring's accounting contact for reconciliation.

Operational caveats and suggestions:
- Recommend limiting retroactive true-ups to one prior month (unless an agreed exception) to reduce revenue churn exposure.
- If reseller netback is >5% and paid monthly, we may need pre-approval from Finance due to cash-flow implications.

I'll pull draft wording for the private offer terms (discount trigger section + settlement appendix) and drop in the Drive link.

Connor O'Brien
Director, Deal Ops
Redwood Inference
